body.statement: For a rational polynomial system with at most \(s_G\) equalities and weak inequalities, degree at most \(D_G\), coefficient bit length \(O(B)\), and \(k_G\) quantified variables, one-block real quantifier elimination decides feasibility and computes a one-free-variable projection using \(B^{O(1)}(s_GD_G)^{O(k_G)}\) bit operations.  The univariate output degrees are \(D_G^{O(k_G)}\), their coefficient bit lengths are \(B(s_GD_G)^{O(k_G)}\), and nonempty sign cells admit exact real-algebraic sample points within the same asymptotic bounds.

source.locator: Theorems 1.3.1 and 1.3.3, pp. 1003--1005, together with the well-behaved-algorithm and sample-point bounds in Sections 1.2 and 3

attestation.note: Checked against the authors' Journal of the ACM text, including the one-free-variable specialization, existential decision bound, output-degree bound, and integer bit-size convention.
